intended_object: A derivation (proof term) of the modal axiom instance ◇φ → φ in any proof system 𝓢 that has the axiom DiaT (the `HasAxiomDiaT` class). It is an accessor for the class field, named after it.
explanation: The body is just `HasAxiomDiaT.diaT _`. It projects the class field and gives a term of the proof type `𝓢 ⊢ ◇φ ==> φ`. In the Foundation library, `⊢` is a Type of derivations, so this is declared as a `def`. Mathematically, though, it is the lemma "the axiom ◇φ → φ is derivable in 𝓢". It is not a mathematical definition: it is a convenience wrapper that makes the class field usable with φ implicit. Its companion `diaT!` is the Prop-level version of the same statement. Nothing here defines a mathematical notion that could be compared with a textbook definition. Mathlib also has no counterpart, since it has no modal-logic entailment framework.
